metadata.case_name: MA CHAK YAU v. CHAN WAI MAN AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Injury to his low back as a result of the Accident on 20 October 2004.
source: By reason of the Accident, the Plaintiff has suffered injury to his low back.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis, unspecified

injuries.description: Back injury in 1999 from slipping and falling at the Racecourse (pre-existing).
source: The Plaintiff suffered a back injury in 1999, when he slipped and fell at the Racecourse.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis, unspecified

manifestations.description: He feels pain in his low back from time to time on a daily basis.
He feels stiffness and pain in his low back when he tries to bend down when standing.
He could not bend down much.
He feels pain when the weather changes.
He feels pain if he sleeps in a bad position, and needs to change position to ease the pain.
If he walks for more than an hour, his legs would feel tired with ache.
He cannot lift heavy things because of the back pain.
After the Accident, the Plaintiff has also stopped going for morning exercise and swimming as he used to do.

treatments_received: Hospitalisation at Prince of Wales Hospital for 4 days
Physiotherapy assessment on 25 October 2004 (no follow-up sessions attended)

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities (general damages) awarded at HK$80,000. The Plaintiff's pain and disabilities are about 20% more than those he had been suffering from before the Accident; that 20% increase is a result of the back injury suffered by reason of the Accident.
